newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - flat to firmer in spots.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS - flat to firmer in spots.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds mainly were flat in late trade on Thursday, though traders noted high quality issues appeared a touch firmer, as they questioned whether prices already reflected an expected rate hike.
"It certainly--dare I say this and jinx ourselves--maybe, possibly, we are looking at a bottom? We may have found a bid here," said a trader.

The latest comments by the chairman of the central bank, Alan Greenspan, reinforced views the Federal Reserve would tighten monetary policy, raising federal funds by 25 basis points, when its policy-making body meets on March 25. The Treasury yield curve flattened in response, a sign more market participants believed that interest rates would be raised.
In Congressional testimony, Greenspan reiterated that the central bank's policy arm would act pre-emptively to prevent inflation from taking root.

"What we at the Federal Open Market Committee are going to have to judge...is not so much the question of where prices are or have been, but rather what is the state of the economy later this year and into 1998."

But in the municipal market, lower-quality issues did not achieve the same gains as their more popular brethren. "Once you get away from the hot-run type names, the market almost feels like it's down half a point," another trader said.
Secondary market activity picked up as the afternoon wound on but the trader noted that it still looked like a buyers' market.
"We saw a fair amount of cash being put to work in the secondary market but they're not paying up, I can tell you that," he said.

Among the bonds quoted were Texas State Turnpike Authority Dallas North Thruway Revenues of January 2023, which carry a 5-1/4 percent coupon. The issues were bid at 5.81 percent, NET, one basis point higher.
And Jefferson County, Alambama, Sewer Revenues of February 2022, which pay a 5-5/8 percent coupon, were bid at 5.87 percent, NET, down one basis point.

Among the competitive issues sold, Ohio's sale of $282.3 million of Higher Education Capital Facilities Bonds, only had a $21 million balance left in late trade. The offering was won at a net interest cost of 5.06 percent by Goldman Sachs.

Connecticut Housing Finance Authority sold $90 million of revenue bonds that was repriced to 6.20 percent in 2028, according to Goldman Sachs. This was five basis points higher than in the first pricing.
In debt futures, the June municipal contract climbed nine ticks to 113-9/32, while the June Treasury bond futures rose 20 ticks to 108-21/32. The MOB spread was 148 ticks.
